The only way to properly begin this list for me is with SOMA. The pitch is kind of dumb, the hero is incredibly dumb, the interpretation of cloned consciousness as some kind of coinflip transfer is retarded. The only value of the plot elements related to philosophy in SOMA is as some kind of brain teaser material for someone who has never thought about metaphysics, ever. This comic gives you a better introduction of basically everything about the issue, and is 1000 times faster to read: http://existentialcomics.com/comic/1. Also, SOMA is a terrible game with two largely unrelated plot elements, one of which is there to extremely clumsily explain the presence of monsters that should not have been there.

I'm certain plenty of people think The Witness is pretentious trash, but to me the "deeper" meaning is simply too abstract to even be relevant. You can have a blast playing the whole game while not giving a shit about the "story".

The Stanley Parable has a similar problem, although not really the same either. While most of its endings taken separately have relative straightforward underlying interpretations, some of them are simply confusing and the game as a whole is completely incoherent. Any global interpretation is going to contradict itself. Once again, I find that the game is enjoyable regardless.

The Talos Principle asks an irrelevant question, if you consider that it even asks a question to begin with. The setup is kind of nice, but the "to show consciousness, the machine must commit a transgression" trope at the end kind of ruined it for me, even though I could see it coming from a mile away. Doesn't matter, had fun. Also, it's plenty of completely arcane documents that are on the face of it largely unrelated. I'm sure there's some way to link everything into a comprehensive interpretation, but unless you read wikis it's mostly just a collection of scrambled old texts, most of which are difficult to make sense of (in some non-trivial sense) even when considered alone. The forum of robots in the extension is in my opinion slightly better but still lacking any interesting perspective beside some trivial PHI101 stuff. A great game and a great extension, though. It's just slightly better than SOMA in the metaphysics side of things, as it at least tries to not have a completely retarded message.
